newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just up as platinum metals slip.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just up as platinum metals slip.

text.p: A minor turn down in platinum group metal (PGMs) prices halted their upward rush on Wednesday, but gold recovered after slipping on a stronger dollar, dealer said.
Dealers said the PGMs lost momentum on the news that Russia, when it begins exports late this month or next, will ship as much as it did in 1996 in the remaining months of this year.
"There was some selling. People can't go short but they might have reduced their long positions on the news," one dealer said
Palladium fixed at $178.00 per ounce down from $180.50 -- its highest price since its record high fix in April, 1989 -- and platinum was set at $393.50 after $396.00.
Gold fixed at $342.70 up from $342.25 earlier and just off Tuesday's $343.00. The Comex June contract was just $0.20 ahead at $343.60.

Earlier the PGMs led the way higher bringing brisk early buying across the complex and dealers said the market largely dismissed the confirmation of Russian shipments beginning this year within weeks.
"When you're looking at a lease rate of 25 per cent for a month (palladium), nobody is going to sell on something which might happen in a couple of week's time," a dealer said.
He noted that open interest had reached a record level on Nymex (on May 19 at 12,182 lots) and with the price going up, that created a textbook opening for a bull market.

"Basically the funds have all gone long. But if the price doesn't go up, it could be vulnerable," he said, adding that most of the precious metal were finely balanced but would remain volatile, led by the PGMs.

The dollar had a saw-saw afternoon, first firming on a 19-per cent fall in the March U.S. trade gap to $8.5 billion but then being sold into on comments from outgoing Commerce Department Secretary Everett Ehrlich that Japan should not revert to export-led growth.
Comex open interest on silver was almost the opposite of palladium, with big short positions established, making the market vulnerable to any upside spike.
"We are seeing mainly selling so far, so maybe the market wants to follow through and go lower," a dealer said.
Silver was two cents lower at $4.68/$4.70, unchanged from earlier levels.
